concedes: Through the counterexamples-and-logic lens, the revision answers my round-1 refutation. C5 now names only a player who lost the previous game (the winner can no longer choose, so the 104.2a counterexample is gone), the C6/C7 fallback that caused it is removed, and the mixed four-player case (B and C lose together, D later, A wins) is covered by one rule: the earliest losing moment counts and ties go by turn order. The case is limited to free-for-all, so 104.2c cannot turn an early loser into a winner (806.1: players compete as individuals). The draw sentence is untouched (step 6), and a game that ends with all remaining players losing at once is a draw under 104.4a, so it goes to 103.1's draw sentence, not to C5. The tie-break needs a reference point for 'earliest in turn order'; 103.1 supplies one (turn order begins with the starting player of that game), and restarts under 727.1 begin a new game, so they do not blur it. I tried further counterexamples (conceding versus state-based losses, restarts, the first loser leaving the match, 800.4h) and found none that an official source settles against the stipulation; the leftover gaps (such as a first loser who has left the match) are shared with 103.1 itself and are not contradictions.

concede_evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.
If all the players remaining in a game lose simultaneously, the game is a draw.
In Free-for-All multiplayer games, a group of players compete as individuals against each other.
A game that is restarted immediately ends.
